rationale: The Court is most likely to reverse in an opinion by the Chief emphasizing that the Cruel and Unusual Punishments Clause regulates the character and proportionality of punishments, not a shelter-availability, no-lawful-alternative limit on what conduct cities may prohibit. Expect at least one dissent (likely Sotomayor, possibly joined or separately written by Jackson) pressing an as-applied Robinson/Powell-White theory, with some chance of a Thomas or Alito concurrence narrowing Robinson and rejecting any compulsion-based Eighth Amendment doctrine.
